title: Psychology in India — Growth and Development
summary: Modern psychology in India from 1916 (University of Calcutta, N. N. Sen Gupta) through Mysore 1924, professional organisations and journals; phases before and after independence; indigenisation (endogenous vs exogenous).

notes.t: Modern psychology in India began in the early twentieth century and grew through universities, professional organisations and journals.

r: First psychology department — University of Calcutta, under Narendra Nath Sen Gupta
Mysore University psychology department — M.V. Gopalswamy
University of Madras psychology department — G.D. Boaz
University of Patna psychology department — H.P. Maiti
NIMHANS (All India Institute of Mental Health), Bangalore

notes.c: Phases in the development of Indian psychology
r: Acceptance of Western theories and rejection of Eastern influence.
Expansion with an applied focus (guidance, counselling, clinical).
More indigenous theories; acknowledgement of Eastern influences.
Indian Psychology formally established as a branch of psychology at the Conference in Pondicherry.

notes.t: Indigenisation means understanding a phenomenon and applying it in a cultural setting. John Adair played an important role. Two forms are distinguished:

r: Developing knowledge, theories and practices from within a culture, rather than borrowing from external sources.
Adapting and modifying external (often Western) theories to fit local cultural and contextual realities.

notes.t: The first psychology department in India was established at the University of Calcutta in 1916 under Narendra Nath Sen Gupta. Indian Psychology was formally established as a branch in 2002 at the Pondicherry Conference.
